title: Capacity-safe dedicated fleet upgrade: GPU pool draining & autoscaler coordination
creator: Priya Singh
description:
Context:
Redwood Dedicated runs multiple GPU pools (pools per region/tier) that serve customer traffic. Upgrades to the runtime (eg. runtime-2.4) require rolling node-level or pool-level changes that temporarily reduce available capacity. For Dedicated customers with reserved throughput we must ensure upgrades do not violate throughput SLOs or cause prolonged request errors.

Problem statement:
- Current ad-hoc upgrade process drains nodes without coordinating with autoscaling and burst capacity, leading to uneven capacity drops and customer-visible tail latency spikes.
- No standardized rollout gates (progressive canaries, traffic soak windows) tied to capacity-aware metrics.
- Manual intervention required to pause autoscaler or to pre-warm extra capacity; this is error-prone at scale.

Goals:
1) Implement capacity-safe pool draining that guarantees a minimum headroom for live traffic and pre-provisions replacement capacity before eviction.
2) Add autoscaler coordination so upgrades never race scale-ups/downs.
3) Define rollout gates and metrics for automated promotion/rollback (node health, token throughput, p95 latency, error-rate, queue-length per pool).
4) Provide an upgrade tooling service (upgrade-manager) to orchestrate multi-pool, multi-region rollouts with an LTS-aware channel selector.

Proposed design (high level):
- Upgrade-manager service does the following steps per pool:
  1. Evaluate pool health and traffic baseline (5m moving avg).
  2. Request autoscaler to "reserve" N GPUs or set temporary min_replicas to maintain min_capacity_percentage during drain. Autoscaler will reply with acceptance or failure reason.
  3. Mark N nodes as "drain-candidate" and cordon them from new connections. Start incremental session migration and prefix/KV cache handoff where applicable.
  4. Evict workloads from one node at a time using a configured drain_window (default 10m) and verify health metrics remain within gate thresholds.
  5. If a metric breach occurs, pause the rollout and attempt automated mitigation (increase reserved capacity, extend drain_window). If mitigation fails, rollback the node to previous runtime and notify on-call.
- Autoscaler integration: expose a short RPC contract: request_reservation(pool, requested_gpus, hold_until_timestamp) and release_reservation(id). The autoscaler must be able to honor reservations up to a configurable budget per-cluster. This prevents scale-to-zero or aggressive scaling during drains.
- Rollout gates: implemented as policy objects bound to a release channel (stable / lts / canary). Default gate thresholds: p95 latency +10% over baseline, error-rate +0.5% absolute, token throughput drop <= 8%. Gate evaluates every minute over a 3-minute window before promoting to next batch.
- LTS & channel logic: customers can pin to an LTS channel (eg. runtime-2.x-stable). Upgrade-manager supports channel-based selection so Dedicated customers on "lts-2026Q1" are only upgraded after channel promotion completes.
- Observability & safety nets: expose per-pool dashboards (reserved capacity, drain-progress, gate-state), synth traffic harness for canaries, and detailed runbook links. Post-upgrade canary evaluation will run BQ/DS metrics comparisons and artifact diff (model/kv compatibility checks).

Testing plan:
- Unit tests around reservation RPC and rollback paths.
- Integration test harness that injects synthetic load and simulates autoscaler latency/failure.
- Staging upgrade against a small dedicated pool with chaos testing (node termination, delayed autoscaler responses).
- Canary rollout in prod to 1% of pools for 24h followed by 10% for 6h before broad rollout.

Rollback & runbook:
- Immediate rollback criteria: queue-length above threshold for >2m, sustained p95 > baseline*1.25 for >5m, or error-rate spike >1% absolute.
- Runbook steps: abort upgrade-manager batch, reprovision capacity, re-add drained node back to service, escalate to infra-oncall, open postmortem in Confluence.
- Playbook link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Dedicated+Upgrade+Runbook

Open decisions & trade-offs:
- Reservation semantics: soft vs hard reservations. Soft reservations are easier (no hard guarantees) but may still allow autoscaler to place other pressure. Hard reservations require autoscaler refactor and capacity accounting. Decision: implement soft reservations for initial rollout and iterate to hard reservations if we observe conflicts.
- Drain concurrency: how many nodes per pool concurrently? Tradeoff between faster rollout and customer risk. Default policy: 1 node per pool for pools < 16 nodes; ceil(N/16) for larger pools.
- Pre-warming vs over-provisioning: prefer pre-warming (quick spin-up of instances) to minimize cost; if spin-up latency is too high in a region, fallback to a short over-provision budget.

- Prototype PR (upgrade-manager core): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4321

Next milestones (owner in parentheses):
- Implement reservation RPC + autoscaler acceptance logic (Diego) - target 2026-03-18
- Upgrade-manager drain orchestration + gate engine (Priya / Diego) - target 2026-03-25
- Staging integr tests + chaos scenarios (SRE) - target 2026-03-29
- Canary in prod (PM & Eng run) - target 2026-04-02

Success criteria:
- No Dedicated customer throughput SLA violations (measured in 7d windows) attributable to the rollout.
- Mean time to rollback <= 10m when automatic rollback triggers.
- Upgrade time per pool reduced vs manual baseline and error rates decreased by >50% vs current ad-hoc process.
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting — aligned on soft reservations first. Action: Diego to mock reservation RPC in autoscaler staging.
2026-03-05: Reviewed gate thresholds with Product (PM: Lina Torres). Reduced default token-throughput drop allowance from 10% -> 8%.
2026-03-07: Prototype PR 4321 created for upgrade-manager main loop. Initial feedback: add per-customer reserved budgets to prevent one customer causing global reservation exhaustion.
2026-03-09: SRE ran local chaos tests; observed autoscaler accepting reservation but delayed by ~90s under control-plane GC — Diego to add retry/backoff and telemetry.
2026-03-10: Decision: drain concurrency default = 1 node; soft reservations will be implemented first. Added security_review_required true and requested sec-review for reservation RPC auth model.
notes: Prefer incremental automation over big-bang refactor. This ticket is the orchestration layer; follow-ups will harden autoscaler accounting and introduce capacity budgets per-customer.
Coordinate with PM Lina Torres for canary windows and customer notifications.
